bill.title: Condemning the violent June 2025 riots in Los Angeles, California.
bill.latestActionText: Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
bill.officialSummary: This resolution expresses gratitude to law enforcement agencies (including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement) with respect to recent demonstrations in Los Angeles, California.

classification.plainSummary: This resolution thanks law enforcement agencies, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, for their response to demonstrations that took place in Los Angeles in June 2025. It is a non-binding expression of gratitude and does not change any law, create new obligations, or allocate funding.

plain.whatItDoes: This resolution would express gratitude to law enforcement agencies (including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement) about recent demonstrations in Los Angeles, California.
plain.whoItTouches: Police officers, and the people they stop.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in how policing works where you live. Nothing has changed yet. This kind of resolution does not become law, even if it passes.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
